Why Patna's air turns toxic every winter

By Guest Columnist

Every winter, Patna's air quality slides into the severe category with depressing regularity, yet enforcement against the known sources remains episodic.

Construction dust, open waste burning and vehicular emissions together account for most of the particulate load, according to the state pollution board's own inventories.

The graded response action plan exists on paper, but stage-wise curbs kick in late and lift early, defeating their purpose.

What the city needs is year-round dust control at construction sites, mechanised street sweeping and a credible public transport alternative.

Until then, residents will keep buying air purifiers while the poorest breathe the worst of it, the author argues.
